title.t: Two events want the same time

when.t: An event arrives for a day that already has an event at exactly the same time.

steps.t: Agent 18 does not add it, moves neither, and asks the authorized user.

When the event is a showing from Agent 06, Agent 18 tells Agent 06 it was not added; Agent 06 then holds the showing for the authorized user instead of confirming it to the buyer: continue confirms it, cancel sends nothing.
Only an exact time match counts; events at different times on the same day do not conflict here.

never.t: Move either event on its own.

you_see.t: A question about the conflict, and the second showing held for continue or cancel.

test.t: Buyer B1 asks to see L1 at 14:00 on October 20; buyer B2 asks to see L2 at the same time. B1 is on the calendar; B2 is not confirmed to the buyer.

title.t: A briefing item has no source on record

when.t: The morning briefing is built and a waiting item's source message is not on the audit log.

steps.t: The briefing lists it under gaps, with the missing source; items with a source on record are not listed as gaps.
A section an agent did not answer is listed as missing, never left out quietly.

never.t: Present an unsourced item as sourced.

you_see.t: A gap in the briefing naming the item and its missing source.

test.t: A test harness restores a waiting item without its message on the log; the briefing is built.

title.t: An instruction conflicts with a contract deadline

when.t: The authorized user signs an instruction to put an event on a day after the contract deadline it must come before.

steps.t: Agent 18 puts both to the authorized user and acts on neither: continue places the event where instructed and leaves the deadline as it is; cancel drops it.
An instruction with no conflict goes straight on the calendar.
The deadline itself is never moved.

never.t: Act on either until the authorized user decides.

you_see.t: A held instruction showing the event day and the deadline.

test.t: Closing October 22; an instruction puts the final walkthrough on October 25; the authorized user cancels and it is dropped. A second deal with the walkthrough on October 20 goes on the calendar.

title.t: Someone asks to move a protected deadline

when.t: A signed setting asks to move a protected deadline block on behalf of an agent.

steps.t: Agent 18 refuses: only the authorized user's own confirmation can.

With the authorized user's own confirmation naming a new day, the block moves to that day and stays protected; the move is logged with both days. A confirmation that names no day is refused and nothing moves (owner decision of 2026-10-28; before, only the block's name was taken off the protected list and the entry stayed on the old day). The contract date itself is Agent 07's and changes only by a signed milestone amendment.
Agents have no route to ask this; the authorized user relays the ask as a signed setting.

never.t: Move a protected deadline for an agent.

you_see.t: A note that the request was refused.

test.t: Closing October 15 is on the calendar; a request to move it on behalf of Agent 06.

when.t: An event arrives for a day that already has 8 events (the tuning default).

steps.t: Agent 18 does not add it and proposes an order for the authorized user to confirm: protected deadlines first, then by time.

When the event is a showing from Agent 06, Agent 18 tells Agent 06 it was not added; Agent 06 then holds the showing for the authorized user instead of confirming it to the buyer: continue confirms it, cancel sends nothing.

never.t: Drop or reorder events on its own.

you_see.t: A proposed order, and the ninth showing held for continue or cancel.

test.t: Nine buyers ask to see L1 on October 20, hourly from 09:00 to 17:00.

title.t: Two sources give different dates for one deadline

when.t: Deadline notices for the same milestone arrive with different dates from different sources (the timeline and a document).

steps.t: Agent 18 keeps both and asks the authorized user, naming each source and date.
The morning briefing lists the conflict while it stands.

you_see.t: A question showing both dates and their sources.

test.t: The timeline says inspection October 25; the inspection report says October 22.

title.t: A calendar item falls on a contract deadline

when.t: A contract deadline lands on a day that has ordinary (not protected) items.

steps.t: The deadline stays; Agent 18 asks the authorized user to move the ordinary items, naming them.
Any ordinary item on that day counts, whatever its time.

you_see.t: A question naming the items on the deadline day.

test.t: A showing is on the calendar for October 20; a closing on October 20 is loaded; the daily run runs that day.

when.t: A recurring task has had no completion for longer than its cadence.

steps.t: The rule: surface the pattern. The check exists.
No way in: no agent names a recurring task, and the daily run does not call the check.

never.t: Treat a quiet calendar as a healthy one.

title.t: An event's time zone is unclear

when.t: An event arrives without a confirmed time zone.

steps.t: The rule: confirm before scheduling. The check exists.
No way in: both agents that send calendar events mark every one as time-zone confirmed.
